prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I get a smooth white wine that isn't sweet at all, tastes like tropical fruit and spices, and is easy to drink while watching a film?"

List A:
Wine 1: Roussanne, US, $22. Tasting note: "Here is a broadly appealing, instantly approachable white wine with mouthwatering flavors of melon, white peach, pineapple and still more exotic tropical fruits. The wine is round and full, forward and just a little tart, but nicely supported with sweet, spicy barrel flavors."
Wine 2: White Blend, US, $20. Tasting note: "The main thing to know about this blend of undisclosed varieties is that it's not dry. It will appeal to consumers who like their white wines fruity and sugary, yet it's not really sweet enough to enjoy as a dessert sipper."
Wine 3: Malagouzia-Chardonnay, Greece, $8. Tasting note: "Tropical fruit aromas and flavors of mango, vanilla and melon give this white blend an exotic spin. Mild acidity gives the wine lift, but the style is easy-drinking and offers a long finish. Pair with poultry or grilled seafood."
Wine 4: Chardonnay, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "Hints of tropical fruit and white peach give this wine a warm, rounded character. It's smooth, with just a shot of acidity and a creamy, spicy texture. Drink now."
Wine 5: Verdejo, Spain, $16. Tasting note: "After opening with white fruit and mineral aromas, this shows a sticky palate made fatter by low acidity. Candied sugary mango, banana and melon flavors are distinctly sweet, which could be a plus or minus depending on your tolerance for residual sugar in a white wine."

List B:
Wine 1: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, US, $32. Tasting note: "Serious white wine. Dense and full-bodied, it's incredibly lush in tropical fruit and apricot flavors. Entirely dry, it shows a honey-sweet layer that's crisp and well-balanced."
Wine 3: Marsanne, US, $12. Tasting note: "Here's a ripe, complex white wine with aromas and flavors ranging from tangerines, apricots and bananas to malted chocolate milk. It tastes very ripe and fruity, with a soft, creamy mouthfeel like peach syrup. There might be just a tad of residual sugar in there, but it's basically a dry wine."
Wine 4: Roussanne, US, $22. Tasting note: "Here is a broadly appealing, instantly approachable white wine with mouthwatering flavors of melon, white peach, pineapple and still more exotic tropical fruits. The wine is round and full, forward and just a little tart, but nicely supported with sweet, spicy barrel flavors."
Wine 5: Bordeaux-style White Blend, France, $20. Tasting note: "The wine is very soft, probably too much so. With a smooth texture, it lacks definition or great fruit. Drink now."
